#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Pair frozen Go App/AppAll builds against all 37 unchanged archived C medians."""
import argparse
from datetime import datetime, timezone
import hashlib
import json
import math
import os
from pathlib import Path
import platform
import runpy
import statistics
import subprocess
import sys

sys.dont_write_bytecode = True
ROOT = Path('/Users/0x1/Documents/htdocs/altbak.pub')
sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT / 'bin/benchmark'))
C = runpy.run_path(str(ROOT / 'bin/benchmark/compare-core.py'))
J = runpy.run_path(str(ROOT / 'bin/benchmark/js-ratios.py'))


def sha(path):
    return hashlib.sha256(Path(path).read_bytes()).hexdigest()


def write(path, value):
    Path(path).write_text(json.dumps(value, ensure_ascii=False, indent=2, allow_nan=False) + '\n')


def metrics(times, reference):
    if set(times) != set(reference) or len(times) not in (14, 37):
        raise ValueError('Identical Go/C case populations of 14 or 37 required')
    ratios = [times[name] / reference[name] for name in times]
    if any(not math.isfinite(x) or x <= 0 for x in ratios):
        raise ValueError('Invalid ratio')
    return {'total': sum(times.values()) / sum(reference.values()),
            'arithmetic': statistics.mean(ratios), 'median': statistics.median(ratios),
            'geometric': math.exp(statistics.mean(math.log(x) for x in ratios))}


def verify_freeze(frozen):
    baseline_path = Path(frozen['compiler_baseline_manifest'])
    if sha(baseline_path) != frozen['compiler_baseline_manifest_sha256']:
        raise ValueError('Compiler baseline manifest changed')
    baseline = json.loads(baseline_path.read_text())
    for group in ['files', 'sources']:
        C['verify_hashes']({entry['path']: entry['sha256'] for entry in baseline[group].values()})
    C['verify_hashes'](frozen['source_sha256'], ROOT)
    C['verify_hashes'](frozen['library_sources_sha256'])
    C['verify_hashes'](frozen['reference_files_sha256'])
    for build in [frozen['go_before_core'], frozen['c_build']]:
        C['verify_hashes']({build['manifest_path']: build['manifest_sha256']})
        C['verify_hashes'](build['payload_sha256'])
    old_all = frozen['go_before_all']
    path = Path(old_all['directory'])
    C['verify_hashes']({str(path / 'manifest.json'): old_all['manifest_sha256'],
                       str(path / 'benchmark'): old_all['manifest']['binary_sha256']})


def compiler_snapshot():
    root = ROOT.parent / 'gopurs/gopurs'
    paths = [root / 'bin/gopurs-native', root / 'bin/gopurs.js', root / 'bin/gopurs']
    paths += [path for folder in ['src', 'runtime'] for path in sorted((root / folder).rglob('*'))
              if path.is_file() and path.suffix in {'.purs', '.go', '.js', '.rs'}]
    return {'root': str(root),
            'head': subprocess.check_output(['git', '-C', str(root), 'rev-parse', 'HEAD'], text=True).strip(),
            'files_sha256': {str(path): sha(path) for path in paths}}


def plan_entry(key, build):
    return {'key': key, 'mode': 'pure', 'command': build['command'],
            'artifact': build['cwd'], 'cwd': build['cwd'],
            'manifest': build['manifest_path'], 'manifest_sha256': build['manifest_sha256'],
            'payload_sha256': build['payload_sha256'],
            'executable_sha256': build['manifest']['binary_sha256']}


def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    parser.add_argument('--freeze', type=Path, default=Path(__file__).with_name('freeze.json'))
    parser.add_argument('--after-core', type=Path, required=True)
    parser.add_argument('--after-all', type=Path, required=True)
    parser.add_argument('--output', type=Path, required=True)
    parser.add_argument('--execute', action='store_true', help='run only after all builds and tests have finished')
    args = parser.parse_args()
    frozen = json.loads(args.freeze.read_text())
    verify_freeze(frozen)
    before_core = C['inspect_go'](Path(frozen['go_before_core']['cwd']))
    after_core = C['inspect_go'](args.after_core.resolve())
    before_all = J['inspect'](Path(frozen['go_before_all']['directory']))
    after_all = J['inspect'](args.after_all.resolve())
    for label, before, after in [('core', before_core['manifest'], after_core['manifest']),
                                 ('all', before_all, after_all)]:
        for field in ['profile', 'toolchain']:
            if before[field] != after[field]:
                raise ValueError(f'{label} build {field} differs')
        for name in before['inputs']:
            if name.startswith(('src/', 'srx/')) and before['inputs'][name] != after['inputs'].get(name):
                raise ValueError(f'{label} benchmark input differs: {name}')
    if before_core['command'] == after_core['command'] or Path(frozen['go_before_all']['directory']) == args.after_all.resolve():
        raise ValueError('Distinct before/after builds are required')
    plan = [plan_entry('before', before_core), plan_entry('after', after_core)]
    if not args.execute:
        print(json.dumps({'validated': True, 'core_plan': plan,
                          'all_pair': [frozen['go_before_all']['directory'], str(args.after_all.resolve())],
                          'C_reference_remeasured': False, 'processes': 12}, indent=2))
        return
    args.output = args.output.resolve()
    args.output.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=False)
    write(args.output / 'freeze.json', frozen)
    write(args.output / 'core-plan.json', plan)
    env = dict(os.environ, GOGC='800')
    for key in ['GOMAXPROCS', 'PPROF']:
        env.pop(key, None)
    compiler = compiler_snapshot()
    started = datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat()
    load_start = list(os.getloadavg())
    commands = [
        [sys.executable, '-B', str(ROOT / 'bin/benchmark/measure.py'), '--plan',
         str(args.output / 'core-plan.json'), '--output', str(args.output / 'core')],
        [sys.executable, '-B', str(Path(__file__).with_name('collect-all.py')), '--before',
         frozen['go_before_all']['directory'], '--after', str(args.after_all.resolve()),
         '--output', str(args.output / 'all')],
    ]
    for command in commands:
        verify_freeze(frozen)
        C['verify_hashes'](compiler['files_sha256'])
        subprocess.run(command, cwd=ROOT, env=env, check=True)
        verify_freeze(frozen)
        C['verify_hashes'](compiler['files_sha256'])
    core = json.loads((args.output / 'core/results.json').read_text())
    all_cases = json.loads((args.output / 'all/results.json').read_text())
    labels = C['ROWS']
    core_times = {variant: dict(zip(labels, data['times_us'])) for variant, data in core.items()}
    core_aggregates = {variant: metrics(times, frozen['c_times_us']) for variant, times in core_times.items()}
    core_historical = metrics(frozen['historical_go_core_times_us'], frozen['c_times_us'])
    for key, value in core_historical.items():
        if not math.isclose(value, frozen['historical_aggregates'][key], rel_tol=1e-12):
            raise ValueError('Historical metrics do not reproduce the official archive')
    # Preserve the publication's primary App medians for core14, and use AppAll
    # for library23 only. Both sides of every aggregate now contain all 37 cases.
    matched37 = {
        variant: {name: core_times[variant][name] if name in core_times[variant]
                  else row['medians_us'][variant]
                  for name, row in all_cases['all_tests'].items()}
        for variant in ('before', 'after')}
    aggregates = {variant: metrics(times, frozen['c37_times_us']) for variant, times in matched37.items()}
    historical = metrics(frozen['historical_go37_times_us'], frozen['c37_times_us'])
    for key, prior_key in [('total', '/'), ('arithmetic', 'μ'), ('median', 'Q₂'), ('geometric', 'G')]:
        if not math.isclose(historical[key], frozen['historical37_aggregates'][prior_key], rel_tol=1e-12):
            raise ValueError('Historical 37-case metrics do not reproduce the official README')
    rows = []
    for name in matched37['after']:
        before, after = matched37['before'][name], matched37['after'][name]
        if name in labels:
            index = labels.index(name)
            samples = {variant: [sample['times_us'][index] for sample in core[variant]['process_runs']]
                       for variant in ['before', 'after']}
        else:
            samples = all_cases['all_tests'][name]['samples_us']
        rows.append({'case': name, 'times_us': {'before': before, 'after': after, 'c': frozen['c37_times_us'][name]},
                     'go_over_c': {variant: times[name] / frozen['c37_times_us'][name] for variant, times in matched37.items()},
                     'samples_us': samples, 'speedup': before / after, 'change_percent': 100 * (after / before - 1),
                     'before_over_historical': before / frozen['historical_go37_times_us'][name]})
    all_regressions = sorted([{'case': name, 'change_percent': case['change_percent'],
                              'medians_us': case['medians_us'], 'samples_us': case['samples_us']}
                             for name, case in all_cases['all_tests'].items() if case['change_percent'] > 5],
                            key=lambda row: -row['change_percent'])
    raw_core = {path.name: path.read_text() for suffix in ['stdout', 'stderr']
                for path in sorted((args.output / 'core').glob('*.' + suffix))}
    report = {'started_at_utc': started, 'completed_at_utc': datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat(),
              'host': platform.platform(), 'machine': platform.machine(), 'host_isolated': False,
              'load_average_start': load_start, 'load_average_end': list(os.getloadavg()),
              'protocol': {'paired_order': 'AB/BA/AB', 'processes_per_build': 3,
                           'primary': '14 App core medians plus 23 AppAll library medians; all four Go/C aggregates use 37 matched cases',
                           'GOGC': '800', 'GOMAXPROCS': 'default', 'pgo': False,
                           'C_reference_remeasured': False, 'JS_reference_remeasured': False,
                           'aggregation': 'median of three process minima for each case'},
              'commands': commands, 'wrapper_sha256': sha(Path(__file__)),
              'frozen_reference': frozen, 'compiler_snapshot': compiler, 'aggregates': aggregates, 'historical_aggregates': historical,
              'primary_times_us': core_times, 'primary_total_ms': {k: sum(v.values())/1000 for k,v in core_times.items()},
              'matched37_times_us': matched37, 'matched37_total_ms': {k: sum(v.values())/1000 for k,v in matched37.items()},
              'core14_aggregates': core_aggregates, 'historical_core14_aggregates': core_historical,
              'c_total_ms': sum(frozen['c37_times_us'].values())/1000,
              'rows_by_go_c_descending': sorted(rows, key=lambda r: -r['go_over_c']['after']),
              'all_case_regressions_over_5_percent': all_regressions,
              'validation': {'processes': 12, 'core_oracles': 84, 'all_oracles': 222,
                             'total_oracles': 306, 'source_and_binary_guards': True},
              'core_manifest': json.loads((args.output / 'core/manifest.json').read_text()),
              'core_campaign': core, 'raw_core_outputs': raw_core, 'all_campaign': all_cases}
    write(args.output / 'results.json', report)
    print(json.dumps({'aggregates': aggregates, 'historical': historical,
                      'totals_ms': report['matched37_total_ms'], 'c_total_ms': report['c_total_ms'],
                      'all_regressions_over_5_percent': all_regressions}, indent=2))


if __name__ == '__main__':
    main()

require(condition, message): if not condition: raise ValueError(message) def sha(data): return hashlib.sha256(data).hexdigest() def json_bytes(value): return (json.dumps(value, ensure_ascii=False, 'count': len(names), 'population': len(times), 'approximate': False, 'cases': names} def campaign_values(campaign, references): require(campaign['validation'] == { 'processes': 12, 'core_oracles': 84, 37 and set(ROWS).issubset(tests), 'Expected 14 core and 23 library AppAll cases') require(all_campaign['order'] == ['before', 'after', 'after', 'before', 'before', 'after'], 'Unexpected AppAll process order') require(set(tests) == set(references), 'JS references must cover exactly the 37 cases') runs = all_campaign['checked_runs'] require(len(runs) == 6 and [run['variant'] for run in runs] == all_campaign['order'], 'Missing checked AppAll processes') for run in runs: result = run['result'] require(result['values_validated'] and len(result['values']) == 14 and result['library']['values_validated'] and len(result['library']['values']) == 23, 'Unvalidated AppAll oracles') for name, case in tests.items(): require(case['js_reference'] == references[name], 'JS reference drift: ' + name) for variant in VARIANTS: samples = case['samples_us'][variant] require(len(samples) == 3, 'Expected three samples: ' + name) close(positive(case['medians_us'][variant]), statistics.median(positive(sample) for sample in samples), name + ' median') # App/AppAll core measurements are different experiments. Publish primary # App medians for the 14 core cases, and AppAll medians for the 23 additions. times = {name: core['after'][name] if name in core['after'] else case['medians_us']['after'] for name, 'Published ' + title + ' timings differ from the frozen references; review before publishing') def review_live_readme(original, frozen): snapshot = WORK / 'README.before.md' baseline = #!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Prepare the report from validated paired data and an implementation summary."""
import argparse, json, sys
from pathlib import Path
sys.dont_write_bytecode = True
WORK = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]
ROOT = WORK.parents[2]
sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT / 'bin/benchmark'))
from publish import format_number

parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
parser.add_argument('--implementation', type=Path, default=WORK / 'implementation.md')
parser.add_argument('--validation', type=Path, default=WORK / 'validation-summary.json')
parser.add_argument('--write', action='store_true', help='write the tracked report only on root authorization')
args = parser.parse_args()
campaign = json.loads((WORK / 'campaign/results.json').read_text())
validation = json.loads(args.validation.read_text())
if validation.get('status') != 'passed':
    raise ValueError('Final validation must be passed')
implementation = args.implementation.read_text().strip()
if implementation.startswith('# '):
    implementation = implementation.partition('\n')[2].strip()
if not implementation:
    raise ValueError('Describe the actual implemented optimization before publication')
refs = ('record/set-small-1000', 'record/set-medium-1000', 'record/set-large-1000')
rows = {row['case']: row for row in campaign['rows_by_go_c_descending']}
lines = ['# Go record update optimization', '', implementation, '',
         'Benchmarks, harnesses, library FFI and C references are unchanged. Runtime inputs remain opaque.', '',
         'This step optimizes conversion from boxed records to native structs. The separate field reads used to sum the original record remain unchanged and remain part of the measured work.', '',
         '## Reference workloads', '',
         '| Case | Official Go baseline (µs) | Paired before (µs) | After (µs) | Speedup in this pair |',
         '| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |']
for name in refs:
    row = rows[name]
    historical = campaign['frozen_reference']['historical_go37_times_us'][name]
    lines.append(f'| `{name}` | {format_number(historical)} | {format_number(row["times_us"]["before"])} | '
                 f'{format_number(row["times_us"]["after"])} | {format_number(row["speedup"])}× |')
lines += ['', '## All 37 matched Go/C cases', '',
          '| Indicator | Official baseline | Paired before | After |',
          '| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |']
for label, key in [('Ratio of totals', 'total'), ('Arithmetic mean μ', 'arithmetic'),
                   ('Median Q₂', 'median'), ('Geometric mean G', 'geometric')]:
    values = [campaign['historical_aggregates'][key], campaign['aggregates']['before'][key], campaign['aggregates']['after'][key]]
    lines.append('| ' + label + ' | ' + ' | '.join(format_number(value) + '×' for value in values) + ' |')
lines += ['', 'All four indicators use the same 37 measured Go/C pairs: 14 core medians from App and 23 library medians from AppAll. '
          'The C denominator remains frozen at ' + str(campaign['c_total_ms']) + ' ms. '
          'Differences between the official baseline and the fresh before measurement reflect measurement variation, not this compiler change.', '',
          '## Measurement and validation', '',
          'Three independent processes per build, in AB/BA/AB order; three global warm-ups, three local warm-ups, '
          'calibrated batches and the minimum of ten batches per process. Published rows use medians across the three processes. '
          'Release Go, GOGC=800, default GOMAXPROCS, no PGO. All builds and tests finish before measurement. The host is not isolated.', '',
          'The App/AppAll campaign validates 306 measured outputs. Source and binary hashes are checked around each collection. '
          'The archived validation summary and runtime-input proofs record the targeted tests, varied inputs, repeatability and opaque-call checks.', '',
          'Full commands, original outputs, compiler changes, input proofs and validation logs are preserved in '
          '[the JSON archive](2026-11-26-go-record-set.json) and `var/benchmark/go-record-set-20261126`.', '']
anomalies = sorted([row for row in campaign['rows_by_go_c_descending'] if row['change_percent'] > 5],
                   key=lambda row: -row['change_percent'])
lines += ['## Regression review', '']
if anomalies:
    lines += ['The primary 37-case combination (App14 and AppAll23) contains these increases above 5%; they are retained in the measurements:', '']
    for row in anomalies:
        lines.append('- `' + row['case'] + '`: +' + format_number(row['change_percent']) + '%.')
    review = WORK / 'regression-review.md'
    if not review.exists() or not review.read_text().strip():
        raise ValueError('Document the regression review before publishing a report with increases above 5%')
    lines += ['', review.read_text().strip(), '']
else:
    lines += ['No published case increased by more than 5% in the primary pair.', '']
    review = WORK / 'regression-review.md'
    if review.exists() and review.read_text().strip():
        lines += [review.read_text().strip(), '']
text = '\n'.join(lines)
preview = WORK / 'report.proposed.md'
preview.write_text(text)
output = ROOT / 'docs/benchmark-results/2026-11-26-go-record-set.md'
if args.write:
    if output.exists():
        raise ValueError('Refusing to overwrite an existing report')
    output.write_text(text)
print(json.dumps({'preview': str(preview), 'report': str(output), 'written': args.write}, indent=2))

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Compare generated source and unchanged build profiles before starting timings."""
import hashlib, json, re, runpy
from pathlib import Path
WORK=Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]
helper=runpy.run_path(str(Path(__file__).with_name('compare-generated.py')))
report={'method':'Exact generated Go sections from source-v1 markers, separate runtime/header checks.',
        'timings_executed':False,'profiles':{}}
for suite in ['core','all']:
    before,after=(WORK/('before-'+suite),WORK/('after-'+suite))
    report[suite]=helper['compare'](before,after)
    manifests=[json.loads((directory/'manifest.json').read_text()) for directory in (before,after)]
    assert manifests[0]['profile']==manifests[1]['profile']
    assert manifests[0]['toolchain']==manifests[1]['toolchain']
    profile=manifests[1]['profile']
    assert profile['GOGC']=='800' and profile['pgo'] is False
    assert profile['backend_profile']=='release'
    assert profile['GOFLAGS']=='' and profile['GOEXPERIMENT']==''
    report['profiles'][suite]={'identical':True,'profile':profile,'toolchain':manifests[1]['toolchain']}
old=helper['inventory'](WORK/'before-all')['sections']
new=helper['inventory'](WORK/'after-all')['sections']
report['targets']={}
for name in ['RecordSetSmall1000','RecordSetMedium1000','RecordSetLarge1000']:
    token=('func Get_Test_'+name+'_prepare(').encode()
    selected={side:[(key,data) for key,data in sections.items() if token in data]
              for side,sections in [('before',old),('after',new)]}
    assert len(selected['before'])==len(selected['after'])==1
    before_key,before=selected['before'][0]
    after_key,after=selected['after'][0]
    assert b'Get_Bench_opaque()' in after
    if name=='RecordSetSmall1000':
        assert before==after, 'Small prepare section changed'
    else:
        assert b'recordProjection_data' in after and b'RecordGet(orig,' in after
        projection=lambda text: re.findall(rb'(?:r_|r|gopurs_runtime)\.RecordGet\(__local_var_[^)]*\)\.IntVal',text)
        assert projection(before) and projection(before)==projection(after), 'Original-record sum reads changed'
    report['targets'][name]={'before_section':before_key,'after_section':after_key,
        'before_sha256':hashlib.sha256(before).hexdigest(),'after_sha256':hashlib.sha256(after).hexdigest(),
        'changed':before!=after,'opaque_preserved':True,
        'record_projection':b'recordProjection_data' in after,'original_sum_reads_unchanged':True}
additional={}
for suite in ['core','all']:
    key='purescript/p_root/Control_Bind.go'
    row=report[suite]['sections']['sha256'][key]
    deleted=[line for line in row['diff'].splitlines() if line.startswith('-') and not line.startswith('---')]
    assert not deleted
    assert 'len(recordProjection_data.Keys) == 7' in row['diff']
    additional[suite]={'section':key,'function':'Rebox_Control_Bind_3094389156_3302008615',
        'fields':['day','hour','millisecond','minute','month','second','year'],
        'change':'Additional guarded canonical RecordData projection; existing fallback retained',
        'deleted_source_lines':0}
report['additional_projection']=additional
output=WORK/'proofs/generated-comparison.json'
output.write_text(json.dumps(report,indent=2)+'\n')
print(json.dumps({'output':str(output),'profiles':report['profiles'],'targets':report['targets'],
                  'core_changed':report['core']['scope_check'],'all_changed':report['all']['scope_check']},indent=2))

 if name=='Test_RecordSetSmall1000':

executed.append(driver['logged'](commands[3], project, logs / 'go-build.log', environment))

(destination / 'stderr.txt').write_text(result.stderr)
expected = '1006\n1072\n1272\n'
(destination / 'expected.txt').write_text(expected)
assert result.stdout == expected and result.stderr == ''
pair['C']['verify_hashes'](compiler['files_sha256'])
pair['verify_freeze'](frozen)

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Read-only independent consistency checks for the archived record update campaign."""
import hashlib, json, runpy, sys
from pathlib import Path
sys.dont_write_bytecode = True
WORK = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]
ROOT = WORK.parents[2]
path = ROOT / 'docs/benchmark-results/2026-11-26-go-record-set.json'
raw = path.read_bytes()
archive = json.loads(raw)
sha = lambda data: hashlib.sha256(data).hexdigest()
count = 0


def visit(value):
    global count
    if isinstance(value, dict):
        if isinstance(value.get('text'), str) and 'sha256' in value:
            assert sha(value['text'].encode()) == value['sha256']
            count += 1
        for child in value.values():
            visit(child)
    elif isinstance(value, list):
        for child in value:
            visit(child)


visit(archive)
helper = runpy.run_path(str(Path(__file__).with_name('archive.py')))
checks = helper['check_campaign'](archive['campaign'])
assert checks == archive['validation']['archive_checks']
assert helper['check_inputs'](archive['campaign']) == archive['validation']['runtime_input_proofs']
assert helper['check_diagnostics'](archive['campaign']) == archive['validation']['diagnostic_checks']
assert archive['validation']['final_summary'] == json.loads((WORK / 'validation-summary.json').read_text())
assert archive['report']['text'] == (ROOT / archive['report']['path']).read_text()
for name, evidence in archive['validation']['logs'].items():
    assert sha((WORK / name).read_bytes()) == evidence['sha256'], name
for name, evidence in archive['proofs']['runtime_inputs_and_collectors'].items():
    assert sha((WORK / 'proofs' / name).read_bytes()) == evidence['sha256'], name
assert not (ROOT / 'bin/benchmark/ratio-measurements.json').exists()
print(json.dumps({'path': str(path), 'bytes': len(raw), 'sha256': sha(raw),
                  'embedded_text_hashes_verified': count, 'campaign': checks,
                  'runtime_oracles': archive['validation']['runtime_input_proofs']['total_oracles'],
                  'removed_catalogue_remains_absent': True}, indent=2))

module Main where

-- @dependencies: prelude effect console refs arrays foldable-traversable

import Prelude
import Data.Array as Array
import Data.Foldable (for_)
import Effect (Effect)
import Effect.Console (logShow)
import Effect.Ref as Ref
import Effect.Unsafe (unsafePerformEffect)

type Pair = { left :: Int, right :: Int }
type Eight = { a :: Int, b :: Int, c :: Int, d :: Int, e :: Int, f :: Int, g :: Int, h :: Int }
type Wide =
  { a :: Int, b :: Int, c :: Int, d :: Int, e :: Int, f :: Int, g :: Int, h :: Int
  , i :: Int, j :: Int, k :: Int, l :: Int, m :: Int, n :: Int, o :: Int, p :: Int }

pairFields :: Pair -> Array Int
pairFields r = [ r.left, r.right ]

eightFields :: Eight -> Array Int
eightFields r = [ r.a, r.b, r.c, r.d, r.e, r.f, r.g, r.h ]

wideFields :: Wide -> Array Int
wideFields r = [ r.a, r.b, r.c, r.d, r.e, r.f, r.g, r.h, r.i, r.j, r.k, r.l, r.m, r.n, r.o, r.p ]

updatePair :: Int -> Pair -> Pair
updatePair 0 r = r
updatePair n r = updatePair (n - 1) (r { right = r.right + 1 })

updateEight :: Int -> Eight -> Eight
updateEight 0 r = r
updateEight n r = updateEight (n - 1) (r { h = r.h + 1 })

updateWide :: Int -> Wide -> Wide
updateWide 0 r = r
updateWide n r = updateWide (n - 1) (r { p = r.p + 1 })

makeWide :: Int -> Wide
makeWide base =
  { a: base, b: base + 1, c: base + 2, d: base + 3
  , e: base + 4, f: base + 5, g: base + 6, h: base + 7
  , i: base + 8, j: base + 9, k: base + 10, l: base + 11
  , m: base + 12, n: base + 13, o: base + 14, p: base + 15 }

-- The reference boundary supplies a boxed record at runtime. Reading all
-- fields of both the old and new record makes destructive reuse observable.
inspectWide :: Int -> Ref.Ref Wide -> Effect (Array (Array Int))
inspectWide count reference = do
  source <- Ref.read reference
  let partial = updateWide count
  pure [ wideFields source, wideFields (partial source), wideFields (partial source), wideFields source ]

inspectEight :: Int -> Ref.Ref Eight -> Effect (Array (Array Int))
inspectEight count reference = do
  source <- Ref.read reference
  pure [ eightFields source, eightFields (updateEight count source), eightFields source ]

inspectPair :: Int -> Ref.Ref Pair -> Effect (Array (Array Int))
inspectPair count reference = do
  source <- Ref.read reference
  pure [ pairFields source, pairFields (updatePair count source), pairFields source ]

type Mixed = { a :: Int, borrowed :: Array Int, nested :: { flag :: Boolean, x :: Int }, shared :: Ref.Ref Int, tag :: String }

typeChanged :: Pair -> { left :: String, right :: Int }
typeChanged source = source { left = "changed" }

type Trace = Ref.Ref (Array Int)

mark :: Trace -> Int -> Int -> Int
mark trace tag value = unsafePerformEffect do
  Ref.modify_ (\events -> Array.snoc events tag) trace
  pure value

markAfter :: Trace -> Int -> Int -> Int
markAfter trace previous value = unsafePerformEffect do
  Ref.modify_ (\events -> Array.snoc events (200 + previous)) trace
  pure value

sourceFactory :: Trace -> Wide -> Wide
sourceFactory trace source = unsafePerformEffect do
  Ref.modify_ (\events -> Array.snoc events 0) trace
  pure source

main :: Effect Unit
main = do
  inputs <- Ref.new
    [ { count: 0, seed: 19 }, { count: 1, seed: -7 }
    , { count: 2, seed: 2147483647 }, { count: 7, seed: -2147483648 }
    , { count: 31, seed: 2147483630 }, { count: 1000, seed: -19 }
    ]
  cases <- Ref.read inputs
  for_ cases \input -> do
    let wide = makeWide input.seed
    wideRef <- Ref.new wide
    eightRef <- Ref.new { a: wide.a, b: wide.b, c: wide.c, d: wide.d, e: wide.e, f: wide.f, g: wide.g, h: wide.h }
    pairRef <- Ref.new { left: wide.a, right: wide.b }
    inspectWide input.count wideRef >>= logShow
    inspectEight input.count eightRef >>= logShow
    inspectPair input.count pairRef >>= logShow
    original <- Ref.read pairRef
    let changed = typeChanged original
    logShow changed.left
    logShow [ original.left, original.right, changed.right ]
  cell <- Ref.new 10
  mixedRef <- Ref.new { a: 17, borrowed: [ 4, 7, 11 ], nested: { flag: true, x: 29 }, shared: cell, tag: "keep λ" }
  source <- Ref.read mixedRef
  let result = source { a = source.a + 3, nested = source.nested { x = source.nested.x + 1 } }
  Ref.write 77 result.shared
  sourceCell <- Ref.read source.shared
  resultCell <- Ref.read result.shared
  logShow [ source.a, result.a, source.nested.x, result.nested.x, sourceCell, resultCell ]
  logShow [ source.borrowed, result.borrowed ]
  logShow [ source.nested.flag, result.nested.flag ]
  logShow source.tag
  logShow result.tag
  trace <- Ref.new []
  traceInput <- Ref.new (makeWide 5)
  observed <- Ref.read traceInput
  let
    original = sourceFactory trace observed
    first = mark trace 1 (original.p + 1)
    second = markAfter trace first (original.a - 1)
    updated = original { p = first, a = second }
  logShow [ wideFields original, wideFields updated, wideFields original ]
  events <- Ref.read trace
  logShow events

module Main where

-- @dependencies: prelude effect console refs arrays foldable-traversable

import Prelude
import Data.Array as Array
import Data.Foldable (for_)
import Effect (Effect)
import Effect.Console (logShow)
import Effect.Ref as Ref
import Effect.Unsafe (unsafePerformEffect)

type Pair = { left :: Int, right :: Int }
type Eight = { a :: Int, b :: Int, c :: Int, d :: Int, e :: Int, f :: Int, g :: Int, h :: Int }
type Wide =
  { a :: Int, b :: Int, c :: Int, d :: Int, e :: Int, f :: Int, g :: Int, h :: Int
  , i :: Int, j :: Int, k :: Int, l :: Int, m :: Int, n :: Int, o :: Int, p :: Int }

pairFields :: Pair -> Array Int
pairFields r = [ r.left, r.right ]

eightFields :: Eight -> Array Int
eightFields r = [ r.a, r.b, r.c, r.d, r.e, r.f, r.g, r.h ]

wideFields :: Wide -> Array Int
wideFields r = [ r.a, r.b, r.c, r.d, r.e, r.f, r.g, r.h, r.i, r.j, r.k, r.l, r.m, r.n, r.o, r.p ]

updatePair :: Int -> Pair -> Pair
updatePair 0 r = r
updatePair n r = updatePair (n - 1) (r { right = r.right + 1 })

updateEight :: Int -> Eight -> Eight
updateEight 0 r = r
updateEight n r = updateEight (n - 1) (r { h = r.h + 1 })

updateWide :: Int -> Wide -> Wide
updateWide 0 r = r
updateWide n r = updateWide (n - 1) (r { p = r.p + 1 })

makeWide :: Int -> Wide
makeWide base =
  { a: base, b: base + 1, c: base + 2, d: base + 3
  , e: base + 4, f: base + 5, g: base + 6, h: base + 7
  , i: base + 8, j: base + 9, k: base + 10, l: base + 11
  , m: base + 12, n: base + 13, o: base + 14, p: base + 15 }

-- The reference boundary supplies a boxed record at runtime. Reading all
-- fields of both the old and new record makes destructive reuse observable.
inspectWide :: Int -> Ref.Ref Wide -> Effect (Array (Array Int))
inspectWide count reference = do
  source <- Ref.read reference
  let partial = updateWide count
  pure [ wideFields source, wideFields (partial source), wideFields (partial source), wideFields source ]

inspectEight :: Int -> Ref.Ref Eight -> Effect (Array (Array Int))
inspectEight count reference = do
  source <- Ref.read reference
  pure [ eightFields source, eightFields (updateEight count source), eightFields source ]

inspectPair :: Int -> Ref.Ref Pair -> Effect (Array (Array Int))
inspectPair count reference = do
  source <- Ref.read reference
  pure [ pairFields source, pairFields (updatePair count source), pairFields source ]

type Mixed = { a :: Int, borrowed :: Array Int, nested :: { flag :: Boolean, x :: Int }, shared :: Ref.Ref Int, tag :: String }

typeChanged :: Pair -> { left :: String, right :: Int }
typeChanged source = source { left = "changed" }

type Trace = Ref.Ref (Array Int)

mark :: Trace -> Int -> Int -> Int
mark trace tag value = unsafePerformEffect do
  Ref.modify_ (\events -> Array.snoc events tag) trace
  pure value

markAfter :: Trace -> Int -> Int -> Int
markAfter trace previous value = unsafePerformEffect do
  Ref.modify_ (\events -> Array.snoc events (200 + previous)) trace
  pure value

sourceFactory :: Trace -> Wide -> Wide
sourceFactory trace source = unsafePerformEffect do
  Ref.modify_ (\events -> Array.snoc events 0) trace
  pure source

main :: Effect Unit
main = do
  inputs <- Ref.new
    [ { count: 0, seed: 19 }, { count: 1, seed: -7 }
    , { count: 2, seed: 2147483647 }, { count: 7, seed: -2147483648 }
    , { count: 31, seed: 2147483630 }, { count: 1000, seed: -19 }
    ]
  cases <- Ref.read inputs
  for_ cases \input -> do

    wideRef <- Ref.new wide
    eightRef <- Ref.new { a: wide.a, b: wide.b, c: wide.c, d: wide.d, e: wide.e, f: wide.f, g: wide.g, h: wide.h }
    pairRef <- Ref.new { left: wide.a, right: wide.b }
    inspectWide input.count wideRef >>= logShow
    inspectEight input.count eightRef >>= logShow
    inspectPair input.count pairRef >>= logShow
    original <- Ref.read pairRef
    let changed = typeChanged original
    logShow changed.left
    logShow [ original.left, original.right, changed.right ]
  cell <- Ref.new 10
  mixedRef <- Ref.new { a: 17, borrowed: [ 4, 7, 11 ], nested: { flag: true, x: 29 }, shared: cell, tag: "keep λ" }
  source <- Ref.read mixedRef
  let result = source { a = source.a + 3, nested = source.nested { x = source.nested.x + 1 } }
  Ref.write 77 result.shared
  sourceCell <- Ref.read source.shared
  resultCell <- Ref.read result.shared
  logShow [ source.a, result.a, source.nested.x, result.nested.x, sourceCell, resultCell ]
  logShow [ source.borrowed, result.borrowed ]
  logShow [ source.nested.flag, result.nested.flag ]
  logShow source.tag
  logShow result.tag
  trace <- Ref.new []
  traceInput <- Ref.new (makeWide 5)
  observed <- Ref.read traceInput
  let
    original = sourceFactory trace observed
    first = mark trace 1 (original.p + 1)
    second = markAfter trace first (original.a - 1)
    updated = original { p = first, a = second }

  logShow events

# 🌈 PureScript universal multi-runtime benchmark ## Project goal This project is a **proof of concept** demonstrating the power of abstraction and portability offered by **PureScript**. The goal is to show how the exact same pure functional code (without any manual FFI) can be compiled and executed natively on radically different ecosystems. Backends consume either standard `CoreFn` or, for the local AOT backends, the typed `TAST/tcorefn` representation exported by a local PureScript fork (may be subject to an official PR soon). ## Comprehensive benchmarks The benchmark suite runs a **wide variety** of computationally intensive tasks: AST evaluation, massive list processing, tail call optimization, deep record updates... These tests apply massive **pressure** on the call stack, garbage collector, disk I/O, event loops, and runtime execution engines to measure the raw ability of the compiler and the underlying virtual machine. > [!NOTE] > **Reading the benchmark tables** > > - **Status, only for gopurs, purust, phpurs, sharpurs and javapurs:** **Stable** = measured and considered fully optimized; **WIP** = measured, with optimization work remaining; **Backlog** = planned work without a published measurement or ratio. Status labels belong only to the relevant backend columns. References and external backends have no status. Stable is currently empty, including for Go: the available analyses still identify optimization opportunities. > - **Ratios:** `/C` uses the optimized imperative C reference; `/JS` uses the first JavaScript column. **Below 1× is faster; above 1× is slower.** Extended Results uses its own JS reference and has no C reference. > - **Totals:** sums of the available per-test medians: **Total WIP** for the controlled backends, **Total** for references and external backends. Backlog never contributes. Empty Stable groups are shown as *Coming soon...* and have no defined total, ratio or mean. These totals do not represent an application benchmark. > - **Summaries:** `μ` = arithmetic mean, `Q₂` = median, `G` = geometric mean of the case ratios. Each case has equal weight. All four ratios use exactly the same measured cases on both sides: Go/C and Go/JS both cover all 37 measured Go cases. The full total of a reference table is not used as a denominator for a different set of cases. Very small reference times can produce large ratios. > - **Missing data:** `—` means unavailable or not applicable, never zero. Bounds (`< …`) are excluded from summaries. `n=a/b` indicates coverage: measured cases out of listed cases for a time total, or matched references out of measured cases for a ratio. Historical diagnostic measurements remain in the reference tables; their controlled-backend counterparts belong to unmeasured Backlog. > - **Display precision, in every table:** values ≥ 1 use two decimal places (`12.000045 → 12.00`); positive values < 1 keep two significant digits after leading zeros (`0.000045`, `0.009492 → 0.0095`). Zero is `0.00`. > - **Opaque inputs, in every table:** inputs must remain unknown to the optimizer at runtime. Algebraic simplification is allowed; substituting the driver’s known input is not. > - **Calculations:** use archived timings before display rounding, including for threshold checks. `≈` marks a fallback to published precision. ### Core stresstest benchmark results (pure computational) **Core tests (`src/`)** cover features common to all tested targets (`./bin/run`) #### JavaScript JS Benchmark | Hand-written PureScript

# 🌈 PureScript universal multi-runtime benchmark ## Project goal This project is a **proof of concept** demonstrating the power of abstraction and portability offered by **PureScript**. The goal is to show how the exact same pure functional code (without any manual FFI) can be compiled and executed natively on radically different ecosystems. Backends consume either standard `CoreFn` or, for the local AOT backends, the typed `TAST/tcorefn` representation exported by a local PureScript fork (may be subject to an official PR soon). ## Comprehensive benchmarks The benchmark suite runs a **wide variety** of computationally intensive tasks: AST evaluation, massive list processing, tail call optimization, deep record updates... These tests apply massive **pressure** on the call stack, garbage collector, disk I/O, event loops, and runtime execution engines to measure the raw ability of the compiler and the underlying virtual machine. > [!NOTE] > **Reading the benchmark tables** > > - **Status, only for gopurs, purust, phpurs, sharpurs and javapurs:** **Stable** = measured and considered fully optimized; **WIP** = measured, with optimization work remaining; **Backlog** = planned work without a published measurement or ratio. Status labels belong only to the relevant backend columns. References and external backends have no status. Stable is currently empty, including for Go: the available analyses still identify optimization opportunities. > - **Ratios:** `/C` uses the optimized imperative C reference; `/JS` uses the first JavaScript column. **Below 1× is faster; above 1× is slower.** Extended Results uses its own JS reference and has no C reference. > - **Totals:** sums of the available per-test medians: **Total WIP** for the controlled backends, **Total** for references and external backends. Backlog never contributes. Empty Stable groups are shown as *Coming soon...* and have no defined total, ratio or mean. These totals do not represent an application benchmark. > - **Summaries:** `μ` = arithmetic mean, `Q₂` = median, `G` = geometric mean of the case ratios. Each case has equal weight. All four ratios use exactly the same measured cases on both sides: Go/C and Go/JS both cover all 37 measured Go cases. The full total of a reference table is not used as a denominator for a different set of cases. Very small reference times can produce large ratios. > - **Missing data:** `—` means unavailable or not applicable, never zero. Bounds (`< …`) are excluded from summaries. `n=a/b` indicates coverage: measured cases out of listed cases for a time total, or matched references out of measured cases for a ratio. Historical diagnostic measurements remain in the reference tables; their controlled-backend counterparts belong to unmeasured Backlog. > - **Display precision, in every table:** values ≥ 1 use two decimal places (`12.000045 → 12.00`); positive values < 1 keep two significant digits after leading zeros (`0.000045`, `0.009492 → 0.0095`). Zero is `0.00`. > - **Opaque inputs, in every table:** inputs must remain unknown to the optimizer at runtime. Algebraic simplification is allowed; substituting the driver’s known input is not. > - **Calculations:** use archived timings before display rounding, including for threshold checks. `≈` marks a fallback to published precision. ### Core stresstest benchmark results (pure computational) **Core tests (`src/`)** cover features common to all tested targets (`./bin/run`) #### JavaScript JS Benchmark | Hand-written PureScript

# 🌈 PureScript universal multi-runtime benchmark ## Project goal This project is a **proof of concept** demonstrating the power of abstraction and portability offered by **PureScript**. The goal is to show how the exact same pure functional code (without any manual FFI) can be compiled and executed natively on radically different ecosystems. Backends consume either standard `CoreFn` or, for the local AOT backends, the typed `TAST/tcorefn` representation exported by a local PureScript fork (may be subject to an official PR soon). ## Comprehensive benchmarks The benchmark suite runs a **wide variety** of computationally intensive tasks: AST evaluation, massive list processing, tail call optimization, deep record updates... These tests apply massive **pressure** on the call stack, garbage collector, disk I/O, event loops, and runtime execution engines to measure the raw ability of the compiler and the underlying virtual machine. > [!NOTE] > **Reading the benchmark tables** > > - **Status, only for gopurs, purust, phpurs, sharpurs and javapurs:** **Stable** = measured and considered fully optimized; **WIP** = measured, with optimization work remaining; **Backlog** = planned work without a published measurement or ratio. Status labels belong only to the relevant backend columns. References and external backends have no status. Stable is currently empty, including for Go: the available analyses still identify optimization opportunities. > - **Ratios:** `/C` uses the optimized imperative C reference; `/JS` uses the first JavaScript column. **Below 1× is faster; above 1× is slower.** Extended Results uses its own JS reference and has no C reference. > - **Totals:** sums of the available per-test medians: **Total WIP** for the controlled backends, **Total** for references and external backends. Backlog never contributes. Empty Stable groups are shown as *Coming soon...* and have no defined total, ratio or mean. These totals do not represent an application benchmark. > - **Summaries:** `μ` = arithmetic mean, `Q₂` = median, `G` = geometric mean of the case ratios. Each case has equal weight. All four ratios use exactly the same measured cases on both sides: Go/C and Go/JS both cover all 37 measured Go cases. The full total of a reference table is not used as a denominator for a different set of cases. Very small reference times can produce large ratios. > - **Missing data:** `—` means unavailable or not applicable, never zero. Bounds (`< …`) are excluded from summaries. `n=a/b` indicates coverage: measured cases out of listed cases for a time total, or matched references out of measured cases for a ratio. Historical diagnostic measurements remain in the reference tables; their controlled-backend counterparts belong to unmeasured Backlog. > - **Display precision, in every table:** values ≥ 1 use two decimal places (`12.000045 → 12.00`); positive values < 1 keep two significant digits after leading zeros (`0.000045`, `0.009492 → 0.0095`). Zero is `0.00`. > - **Opaque inputs, in every table:** inputs must remain unknown to the optimizer at runtime. Algebraic simplification is allowed; substituting the driver’s known input is not. > - **Calculations:** use archived timings before display rounding, including for threshold checks. `≈` marks a fallback to published precision. ### Core stresstest benchmark results (pure computational) **Core tests (`src/`)** cover features common to all tested targets (`./bin/run`) #### JavaScript JS Benchmark | Hand-written PureScript

# 🌈 PureScript universal multi-runtime benchmark ## Project goal This project is a **proof of concept** demonstrating the power of abstraction and portability offered by **PureScript**. The goal is to show how the exact same pure functional code (without any manual FFI) can be compiled and executed natively on radically different ecosystems. Backends consume either standard `CoreFn` or, for the local AOT backends, the typed `TAST/tcorefn` representation exported by a local PureScript fork (may be subject to an official PR soon). ## Comprehensive benchmarks The benchmark suite runs a **wide variety** of computationally intensive tasks: AST evaluation, massive list processing, tail call optimization, deep record updates... These tests apply massive **pressure** on the call stack, garbage collector, disk I/O, event loops, and runtime execution engines to measure the raw ability of the compiler and the underlying virtual machine. > [!NOTE] > **Reading the benchmark tables** > > - **Status, only for gopurs, purust, phpurs, sharpurs and javapurs:** **Stable** = measured and considered fully optimized; **WIP** = measured, with optimization work remaining; **Backlog** = planned work without a published measurement or ratio. Status labels belong only to the relevant backend columns. References and external backends have no status. Stable is currently empty, including for Go: the available analyses still identify optimization opportunities. > - **Ratios:** `/C` uses the optimized imperative C reference; `/JS` uses the first JavaScript column. **Below 1× is faster; above 1× is slower.** Extended Results uses its own JS reference and has no C reference. > - **Totals:** sums of the available per-test medians: **Total WIP** for the controlled backends, **Total** for references and external backends. Backlog never contributes. Empty Stable groups are shown as *Coming soon...* and have no defined total, ratio or mean. These totals do not represent an application benchmark. > - **Summaries:** `μ` = arithmetic mean, `Q₂` = median, `G` = geometric mean of the case ratios. Each case has equal weight. All four ratios use exactly the same measured cases on both sides: Go/C and Go/JS both cover all 37 measured Go cases. The full total of a reference table is not used as a denominator for a different set of cases. Very small reference times can produce large ratios. > - **Missing data:** `—` means unavailable or not applicable, never zero. Bounds (`< …`) are excluded from summaries. `n=a/b` indicates coverage: measured cases out of listed cases for a time total, or matched references out of measured cases for a ratio. Historical diagnostic measurements remain in the reference tables; their controlled-backend counterparts belong to unmeasured Backlog. > - **Display precision, in every table:** values ≥ 1 use two decimal places (`12.000045 → 12.00`); positive values < 1 keep two significant digits after leading zeros (`0.000045`, `0.009492 → 0.0095`). Zero is `0.00`. > - **Opaque inputs, in every table:** inputs must remain unknown to the optimizer at runtime. # 🌈 PureScript universal multi-runtime benchmark ## Project goal This project is a **proof of concept** demonstrating the power of abstraction and portability offered by **PureScript**. The goal is to show how the exact same pure functional code (without any manual FFI) can be compiled and executed natively on radically different ecosystems. Backends consume either standard `CoreFn` or, for the local AOT backends, the typed `TAST/tcorefn` representation exported by a local PureScript fork (may be subject to an official PR soon). ## Comprehensive benchmarks The benchmark suite runs a **wide variety** of computationally intensive tasks: AST evaluation, massive list processing, tail call optimization, deep record updates... These tests apply massive **pressure** on the call stack, garbage collector, disk I/O, event loops, and runtime execution engines to measure the raw ability of the compiler and the underlying virtual machine. > [!NOTE] > **Reading the benchmark tables** > > - **Status, only for gopurs, purust, phpurs, sharpurs and javapurs:** **Stable** = measured and considered fully optimized; **WIP** = measured, with optimization work remaining; **Backlog** = planned work without a published measurement or ratio. Status labels belong only to the relevant backend columns. References and external backends have no status. Stable is currently empty, including for Go: the available analyses still identify optimization opportunities. > - **Ratios:** `/C` uses the optimized imperative C reference; `/JS` uses the first JavaScript column. **Below 1× is faster; above 1× is slower.** Extended Results uses its own JS reference and has no C reference. > - **Totals:** sums of the available per-test medians: **Total WIP** for the controlled backends, **Total** for references and external backends. Backlog never contributes. Empty Stable groups are shown as *Coming soon...* and have no defined total, ratio or mean. These totals do not represent an application benchmark. > - **Summaries:** `μ` = arithmetic mean, `Q₂` = median, `G` = geometric mean of the case ratios. Each case has equal weight. All four ratios use exactly the same measured cases on both sides: Go/C and Go/JS both cover all 37 measured Go cases. The full total of a reference table is not used as a denominator for a different set of cases. Very small reference times can produce large ratios. > - **Missing data:** `—` means unavailable or not applicable, never zero. Bounds (`< …`) are excluded from summaries. `n=a/b` indicates coverage: measured cases out of listed cases for a time total, or matched references out of measured cases for a ratio. Historical diagnostic measurements remain in the reference tables; their controlled-backend counterparts belong to unmeasured Backlog. > - **Display precision, in every table:** values ≥ 1 use two decimal places (`12.000045 → 12.00`); positive values < 1 keep two significant digits after leading zeros (`0.000045`, `0.009492 → 0.0095`). Zero is `0.00`. > - **Opaque inputs, in every table:** inputs must remain unknown to the optimizer at runtime. Algebraic simplification is allowed; substituting the driver’s known input is not. > - **Calculations:** use archived timings before display rounding, including for threshold checks. `≈` marks a fallback to published precision. ### Core stresstest benchmark results (pure computational) **Core tests (`src/`)** cover features common to all tested targets (`./bin/run`) #### JavaScript JS Benchmark | Hand-written PureScript

# 🌈 PureScript universal multi-runtime benchmark ## Project goal This project is a **proof of concept** demonstrating the power of abstraction and portability offered by **PureScript**. The goal is to show how the exact same pure functional code (without any manual FFI) can be compiled and executed natively on radically different ecosystems. Backends consume either standard `CoreFn` or, for the local AOT backends, the typed `TAST/tcorefn` representation exported by a local PureScript fork (may be subject to an official PR soon). ## Comprehensive benchmarks The benchmark suite runs a **wide variety** of computationally intensive tasks: AST evaluation, massive list processing, tail call optimization, deep record updates... These tests apply massive **pressure** on the call stack, garbage collector, disk I/O, event loops, and runtime execution engines to measure the raw ability of the compiler and the underlying virtual machine. > [!NOTE] > **Reading the benchmark tables** > > - **Status, only for gopurs, purust, phpurs, sharpurs and javapurs:** **Stable** = measured and considered fully optimized; **WIP** = measured, with optimization work remaining; **Backlog** = planned work without a published measurement or ratio. Status labels belong only to the relevant backend columns. References and external backends have no status. Stable is currently empty, including for Go: the available analyses still identify optimization opportunities. > - **Ratios:** `/C` uses the optimized imperative C reference; `/JS` uses the first JavaScript column. **Below 1× is faster; above 1× is slower.** Extended Results uses its own JS reference and has no C reference. > - **Totals:** sums of the available per-test medians: **Total WIP** for the controlled backends, **Total** for references and external backends. Backlog never contributes. Empty Stable groups are shown as *Coming soon...* and have no defined total, ratio or mean. These totals do not represent an application benchmark. > - **Summaries:** `μ` = arithmetic mean, `Q₂` = median, `G` = geometric mean of the case ratios. Each case has equal weight. All four ratios use exactly the same measured cases on both sides: Go/C and Go/JS both cover all 37 measured Go cases. The full total of a reference table is not used as a denominator for a different set of cases. Very small reference times can produce large ratios. > - **Missing data:** `—` means unavailable or not applicable, never zero. Bounds (`< …`) are excluded from summaries. `n=a/b` indicates coverage: measured cases out of listed cases for a time total, or matched references out of measured cases for a ratio. Historical diagnostic measurements remain in the reference tables; their controlled-backend counterparts belong to unmeasured Backlog. > - **Display precision, in every table:** values ≥ 1 use two decimal places (`12.000045 → 12.00`); positive values < 1 keep two significant digits after leading zeros (`0.000045`, `0.009492 → 0.0095`). Zero is `0.00`. > - **Opaque inputs, in every table:** inputs must remain unknown to the optimizer at runtime. Algebraic simplification is allowed; substituting the driver’s known input is not. > - **Calculations:** use archived timings before display rounding, including for threshold checks. `≈` marks a fallback to published precision. ### Core stresstest benchmark results (pure computational) **Core tests (`src/`)** cover features common to all tested targets (`./bin/run`) #### JavaScript JS Benchmark | Hand-written PureScript

# 🌈 PureScript universal multi-runtime benchmark ## Project goal This project is a **proof of concept** demonstrating the power of abstraction and portability offered by **PureScript**. The goal is to show how the exact same pure functional code (without any manual FFI) can be compiled and executed natively on radically different ecosystems. Backends consume either standard `CoreFn` or, for the local AOT backends, the typed `TAST/tcorefn` representation exported by a local PureScript fork (may be subject to an official PR soon). ## Comprehensive benchmarks The benchmark suite runs a **wide variety** of computationally intensive tasks: AST evaluation, massive list processing, tail call optimization, deep record updates... These tests apply massive **pressure** on the call stack, garbage collector, disk I/O, event loops, and runtime execution engines to measure the raw ability of the compiler and the underlying virtual machine. > [!NOTE] > **Reading the benchmark tables** > > - **Status, only for gopurs, purust, phpurs, sharpurs and javapurs:** **Stable** = measured and considered fully optimized; **WIP** = measured, with optimization work remaining; **Backlog** = planned work without a published measurement or ratio. Status labels belong only to the relevant backend columns. References and external backends have no status. Stable is currently empty, including for Go: the available analyses still identify optimization opportunities. > - **Ratios:** `/C` uses the optimized imperative C reference; `/JS` uses the first JavaScript column. **Below 1× is faster; above 1× is slower.** Extended Results uses its own JS reference and has no C reference. > - **Totals:** sums of the available per-test medians: **Total WIP** for the controlled backends, **Total** for references and external backends. Backlog never contributes. Empty Stable groups are shown as *Coming soon...* and have no defined total, ratio or mean. These totals do not represent an application benchmark. > - **Summaries:** `μ` = arithmetic mean, `Q₂` = median, `G` = geometric mean of the case ratios. Each case has equal weight. All four ratios use exactly the same measured cases on both sides: Go/C and Go/JS both cover all 37 measured Go cases. The full total of a reference table is not used as a denominator for a different set of cases. Very small reference times can produce large ratios. > - **Missing data:** `—` means unavailable or not applicable, never zero. Bounds (`< …`) are excluded from summaries. `n=a/b` indicates coverage: measured cases out of listed cases for a time total, or matched references out of measured cases for a ratio. Historical diagnostic measurements remain in the reference tables; their controlled-backend counterparts belong to unmeasured Backlog. > - **Display precision, in every table:** values ≥ 1 use two decimal places (`12.000045 → 12.00`); positive values < 1 keep two significant digits after leading zeros (`0.000045`, `0.009492 → 0.0095`). Zero is `0.00`. > - **Opaque inputs, in every table:** inputs must remain unknown to the optimizer at runtime. Algebraic simplification is allowed; substituting the driver’s known input is not. > - **Calculations:** use archived timings before display rounding, including for threshold checks. `≈` marks a fallback to published precision. ### Core stresstest benchmark results (pure computational) **Core tests (`src/`)** cover features common to all tested targets (`./bin/run`) #### JavaScript JS Benchmark | Hand-written PureScript

# 🌈 PureScript universal multi-runtime benchmark ## Project goal This project is a **proof of concept** demonstrating the power of abstraction and portability offered by **PureScript**. The goal is to show how the exact same pure functional code (without any manual FFI) can be compiled and executed natively on radically different ecosystems. Backends consume either standard `CoreFn` or, for the local AOT backends, the typed `TAST/tcorefn` representation exported by a local PureScript fork (may be subject to an official PR soon). ## Comprehensive benchmarks The benchmark suite runs a **wide variety** of computationally intensive tasks: AST evaluation, massive list processing, tail call optimization, deep record updates... These tests apply massive **pressure** on the call stack, garbage collector, disk I/O, event loops, and runtime execution engines to measure the raw ability of the compiler and the underlying virtual machine. > [!NOTE] > **Reading the benchmark tables** > > - **Status, only for gopurs, purust, phpurs, sharpurs and javapurs:** **Stable** = measured and considered fully optimized; **WIP** = measured, with optimization work remaining; **Backlog** = planned work without a published measurement or ratio. Status labels belong only to the relevant backend columns. References and external backends have no status. Stable is currently empty, including for Go: the available analyses still identify optimization opportunities. > - **Ratios:** `/C` uses the optimized imperative C reference; `/JS` uses the first JavaScript column. **Below 1× is faster; above 1× is slower.** Extended Results uses its own JS reference and has no C reference. > - **Totals:** sums of the available per-test medians: **Total WIP** for the controlled backends, **Total** for references and external backends. Backlog never contributes. Empty Stable groups are shown as *Coming soon...* and have no defined total, ratio or mean. These totals do not represent an application benchmark. > - **Summaries:** `μ` = arithmetic mean, `Q₂` = median, `G` = geometric mean of the case ratios. Each case has equal weight. All four ratios use exactly the same measured cases on both sides: Go/C and Go/JS both cover all 37 measured Go cases. The full total of a reference table is not used as a denominator for a different set of cases. Very small reference times can produce large ratios. > - **Missing data:** `—` means unavailable or not applicable, never zero. Bounds (`< …`) are excluded from summaries. `n=a/b` indicates coverage: measured cases out of listed cases for a time total, or matched references out of measured cases for a ratio. Historical diagnostic measurements remain in the reference tables; their controlled-backend counterparts belong to unmeasured Backlog. > - **Display precision, in every table:** values ≥ 1 use two decimal places (`12.000045 → 12.00`); positive values < 1 keep two significant digits after leading zeros (`0.000045`, `0.009492 → 0.0095`). Zero is `0.00`. > - **Opaque inputs, in every table:** inputs must remain unknown to the optimizer at runtime. Algebraic simplification is allowed; substituting the driver’s known input is not. > - **Calculations:** use archived timings before display rounding, including for threshold checks. `≈` marks a fallback to published precision. ### Core stresstest benchmark results (pure computational) **Core tests (`src/`)** cover features common to all tested targets (`./bin/run`) #### JavaScript JS Benchmark | Hand-written PureScript

campaign/core/README.before.md.text:
# 🌈 PureScript universal multi-runtime benchmark ## Project goal This project is a **proof of concept** demonstrating the power of abstraction and portability offered by **PureScript**. The goal is to show how the exact same pure functional code (without any manual FFI) can be compiled and executed natively on radically different ecosystems. Backends consume either standard `CoreFn` or, for the local AOT backends, the typed `TAST/tcorefn` representation exported by a local PureScript fork (may be subject to an official PR soon). ## Comprehensive benchmarks The benchmark suite runs a **wide variety** of computationally intensive tasks: AST evaluation, massive list processing, tail call optimization, deep record updates... These tests apply massive **pressure** on the call stack, garbage collector, disk I/O, event loops, and runtime execution engines to measure the raw ability of the compiler and the underlying virtual machine. > [!NOTE] > **Reading the benchmark tables** > > - **Status, only for gopurs, purust, phpurs, sharpurs and javapurs:** **Stable** = measured and considered fully optimized; **WIP** = measured, with optimization work remaining; **Backlog** = planned work without a published measurement or ratio. Status labels belong only to the relevant backend columns. References and external backends have no status. Stable is currently empty, including for Go: the available analyses still identify optimization opportunities. > - **Ratios:** `/C` uses the optimized imperative C reference; `/JS` uses the first JavaScript column. **Below 1× is faster; above 1× is slower.** Extended Results uses its own JS reference and has no C reference. > - **Totals:** sums of the available per-test medians: **Total WIP** for the controlled backends, **Total** for references and external backends. Backlog never contributes. Empty Stable groups are shown as *Coming soon...* and have no defined total, ratio or mean. These totals do not represent an application benchmark. > - **Summaries:** `μ` = arithmetic mean, `Q₂` = median, `G` = geometric mean of the case ratios. Each case has equal weight. All four ratios use exactly the same measured cases on both sides: Go/C and Go/JS both cover all 37 measured Go cases. The full total of a reference table is not used as a denominator for a different set of cases. Very small reference times can produce large ratios. > - **Missing data:** `—` means unavailable or not applicable, never zero. Bounds (`< …`) are excluded from summaries. `n=a/b` indicates coverage: measured cases out of listed cases for a time total, or matched references out of measured cases for a ratio. Historical diagnostic measurements remain in the reference tables; their controlled-backend counterparts belong to unmeasured Backlog. > - **Display precision, in every table:** values ≥ 1 use two decimal places (`12.000045 → 12.00`); positive values < 1 keep two significant digits after leading zeros (`0.000045`, `0.009492 → 0.0095`). Zero is `0.00`. > - **Opaque inputs, in every table:** inputs must remain unknown to the optimizer at runtime. Algebraic simplification is allowed; substituting the driver’s known input is not. > - **Calculations:** use archived timings before display rounding, including for threshold checks. `≈` marks a fallback to published precision. ### Core stresstest benchmark results (pure computational) **Core tests (`src/`)** cover features common to all tested targets (`./bin/run`) #### JavaScript JS Benchmark | Hand-written PureScript

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Measure frozen AppAll builds against the exact published JavaScript references.

Without --after, record a three-process baseline. With --after, compare the
two complete suites in AB/BA/AB order. Benchmark sources and harnesses are not
rewritten; this runner only validates and executes the frozen artifacts.
"""
import argparse
from datetime import datetime, timezone
import hashlib
import json
import os
from pathlib import Path
import platform
import statistics
import subprocess
import sys

sys.dont_write_bytecode = True
from library_suite import library_cases
from measure import check
from publish import ROWS
from validate import CASES, validate_output


ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]
CATALOGUE = ROOT / 'bin/benchmark/ratio-measurements.json'
LISTED = (
    'RowToList', 'string/indexOf-hit-10000', 'State Monad',
    'record/set-large-1000', 'record/set-medium-1000', 'effect/ref-write-10000',
    'string/concat-1000', 'AST Evaluation', 'array/map-10000',
)


def sha(path):
    return hashlib.sha256(path.read_bytes()).hexdigest()


def inspect(directory):
    path = directory / 'manifest.json'
    manifest = json.loads(path.read_text())
    expected = {'language': 'go', 'mode': 'pure', 'test': None,
                'entry': 'AppAll', 'include_library': True}
    if any(manifest.get(key) != value for key, value in expected.items()):
        raise ValueError(f'Expected a frozen Go AppAll build: {directory}')
    profile = manifest['profile']
    if profile['backend_profile'] != 'release' or profile['pgo']:
        raise ValueError('Only Release builds without PGO can be compared')
    if sha(directory / 'benchmark') != manifest['binary_sha256']:
        raise ValueError(f'Executable differs from its manifest: {directory}')
    # The native driver records extra diagnostic sources not copied into an
    # AppAll workspace. Verify every recorded live source, every copy present,
    # and explicitly require the complete 37-case suite and its harness.
    for name, digest in manifest['inputs'].items():
        if not name.startswith(('src/', 'srx/')):
            continue
        if sha(ROOT / name) != digest:
            raise ValueError(f'Benchmark source changed since build: {name}')
        copied = directory / name
        if copied.is_file() and sha(copied) != digest:
            raise ValueError(f'Workspace source differs from manifest: {copied}')
    required = ['src/App.purs', 'src/AppAll.purs', 'src/AppLibrary.purs',
                'src/Bench.purs', 'src/Bench.go']
    names = list(CASES) + [case['module'].removeprefix('Test.') for case in library_cases()]
    required += [f'src/Test/{name}/{name}.purs' for name in names]
    for name in required:
        if not (directory / name).is_file():
            raise ValueError(f'Missing suite input: {directory / name}')
        if sha(directory / name) != manifest['inputs'][name]:
            raise ValueError(f'Suite input differs from manifest: {name}')
    oracle = 'bin/benchmark/library-cases.json'
    if sha(ROOT / oracle) != manifest['inputs'][oracle]:
        raise ValueError('Library oracles changed since build')
    return manifest


def definitions():
    if len(CASES) != len(ROWS):
        raise ValueError('Core row names and oracle contract disagree')
    core = [{'name': label, 'module': 'Test.' + module, 'category': 'Stable',
             'expected': int(value)}
            for label, (module, value) in zip(ROWS, CASES.items())]
    library = [{'name': case['label'], 'module': case['module'],
                'category': 'Incl WIP', 'expected': int(case['value'])}
               for case in library_cases()]
    return core + library


def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    parser.add_argument('--before', type=Path, required=True)
    parser.add_argument('--after', type=Path, help='omit for a baseline-only campaign')
    parser.add_argument('--output', type=Path, required=True)
    parser.add_argument('--timeout', type=float, default=600)
    args = parser.parse_args()
    directories = {'before': args.before.resolve()}
    if args.after:
        directories['after'] = args.after.resolve()
        if directories['before'] == directories['after']:
            raise ValueError('Before and after must be distinct frozen builds')
    manifests = {name: inspect(directory) for name, directory in directories.items()}
    manifest_hashes = {name: sha(directory / 'manifest.json') for name, directory in directories.items()}
    if args.after:
        for key in ('profile', 'toolchain'):
            if manifests['before'][key] != manifests['after'][key]:
                raise ValueError(f'Build configurations differ: {key}')
        sources = {name: {key: value for key, value in manifest['inputs'].items()
                          if key.startswith(('src/', 'srx/'))}
                   for name, manifest in manifests.items()}
        if sources['before'] != sources['after']:
            raise ValueError('The benchmark sources differ between builds')
    catalogue_hash = sha(CATALOGUE)
    references = json.loads(CATALOGUE.read_text())['columns']['js-pure']
    cases = definitions()
    if len(cases) != 37 or not set(LISTED).issubset(case['name'] for case in cases):
        raise ValueError('The expected 14 core + 23 library suite changed')
    for case in cases:
        if references[case['name']]['time_us'] <= 0:
            raise ValueError('A positive exact JavaScript reference is required')
    args.output.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=False)
    env = dict(os.environ, GOGC=manifests['before']['profile']['GOGC'])
    env.pop('PPROF', None)
    order = ['before', 'after', 'after', 'before', 'before', 'after'] if args.after else ['before'] * 3
    samples = {name: [] for name in directories}
    raw_output, raw_errors, checked_runs = {}, {}, []
    for index, variant in enumerate(order, 1):
        directory = directories[variant]
        if sha(directory / 'manifest.json') != manifest_hashes[variant]:
            raise ValueError('Build manifest changed during measurement')
        if sha(directory / 'benchmark') != manifests[variant]['binary_sha256']:
            raise ValueError('Executable changed during measurement')
        process = subprocess.run([str(directory / 'benchmark')], cwd=directory,
                                 env=env, capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=args.timeout)
        stem = f'{index}-{variant}'
        (args.output / f'{stem}.log').write_text(process.stdout)
        (args.output / f'{stem}.stderr').write_text(process.stderr)
        process.check_returncode()
        # Require the appended library section, then also validate calibrated
        # power-of-two batch counts through the established campaign checker.
        validate_output(process.stdout, 'pure', include_library=True)
        checked = check(process.stdout, 'pure')
        times = checked['times_us'] + checked['library']['times_us']
        samples[variant].append(times)
        checked_runs.append({'variant': variant, 'result': checked})
        raw_output[stem] = process.stdout
        raw_errors[stem] = process.stderr
        row = dict(zip((case['name'] for case in cases), times))
        print(f'{stem}: 37 oracles verified; RowToList={row["RowToList"]:.6f} us; '
              f'indexOf-hit={row["string/indexOf-hit-10000"]:.6f} us', flush=True)
    all_tests = {}
    for index, case in enumerate(cases):
        name = case['name']
        reference = references[name]
        values = {variant: [run[index] for run in runs] for variant, runs in samples.items()}
        medians = {variant: statistics.median(runs) for variant, runs in values.items()}
        ratios = {variant: elapsed / reference['time_us'] for variant, elapsed in medians.items()}
        item = {**case, 'listed_js_target': name in LISTED,
                'js_reference': reference, 'target_us_strictly_below': 2 * reference['time_us'],
                'samples_us': values, 'medians_us': medians, 'ratios_js': ratios,
                'all_samples_below_2': {variant: max(runs) < 2 * reference['time_us']
                                        for variant, runs in values.items()}}
        if args.after:
            item['speedup'] = medians['before'] / medians['after']
            item['change_percent'] = 100 * (medians['after'] / medians['before'] - 1)
        all_tests[name] = item
    final = 'after' if args.after else 'before'
    listed = sorted(LISTED, key=lambda name: all_tests[name]['ratios_js'][final], reverse=True)
    remaining = [name for name in listed if all_tests[name]['ratios_js'][final] >= 2]
    report = {
        'measured_at_utc': datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat(),
        'host': platform.platform(), 'machine': platform.machine(),
        'mode': 'comparison' if args.after else 'baseline',
        'scope': {'core': 14, 'library': 23, 'listed_js_targets': 9},
        'protocol': 'Three independent processes per variant; AB/BA/AB when comparing; '
                    'three global warmups per suite, three local warmups, calibration, '
                    'minimum of ten batches; median per row of process minima.',
        'order': order, 'GOGC': env['GOGC'], 'GOMAXPROCS': env.get('GOMAXPROCS', 'default'),
        'js_reference_remeasured': False,
        'catalogue': {'path': str(CATALOGUE), 'sha256': catalogue_hash},
        'runner_sha256': sha(Path(__file__)),
        'workspaces': {name: str(path) for name, path in directories.items()},
        'manifest_sha256': manifest_hashes, 'builds': manifests,
        'executable_sha256': {name: manifest['binary_sha256'] for name, manifest in manifests.items()},
        'all_tests': all_tests, 'listed_tests_descending': listed,
        'remaining_listed_at_or_above_2': remaining,
        'remaining_all_at_or_above_2': sorted(
            (name for name, item in all_tests.items() if item['ratios_js'][final] >= 2),
            key=lambda name: all_tests[name]['ratios_js'][final], reverse=True),
        'goal_listed_under_2': not remaining,
        'checked_runs': checked_runs, 'raw_process_output': raw_output,
        'raw_process_stderr': raw_errors,
    }
    for variant, directory in directories.items():
        inspect(directory)
        if sha(directory / 'manifest.json') != manifest_hashes[variant]:
            raise ValueError('Build manifest changed during measurement')
    if sha(CATALOGUE) != catalogue_hash:
        raise ValueError('JavaScript references changed during measurement')
    (args.output / 'results.json').write_text(json.dumps(report, indent=2) + '\n')
    print(json.dumps({name: {'us': all_tests[name]['medians_us'][final],
                            'ratio_js': all_tests[name]['ratios_js'][final]}
                      for name in listed}, indent=2))


if __name__ == '__main__':
    try:
        main()
